notes: Customer summary: Novara builds clinical decision-support tools for hospitals; PHI touches so they require strict residency and encryption controls.
Primary ask: Private VPC deployment with full control of encryption keys, integration with their enterprise KMS (AWS KMS + CloudHSM currently), and comprehensive audit trail forwarding to Splunk.
In-transit requirements (from SecOps): mutual TLS (mTLS) between Novara app hosts and Redwood inference endpoints; client certs managed by their PKI; prefer SPIFFE/SPIRE for short-lived certs.
TLS constraints: enforce TLS1.3 only, disallow legacy ciphers, prefer AEAD ciphers; renegotiation disallowed. Must support perfect forward secrecy.

TLS termination: no public termination in Redwood-managed plane for private deployment — they want TLS end-to-end to the inference nodes inside their VPC (Redwood Private that runs control plane but data plane in-customer VPC).

At-rest requirements: disk-level encryption on inference nodes (dm-crypt/LUKS on on-prem), encrypted EBS with AWS CMKs for cloud; all token caches and KV caches must be encrypted with envelope encryption using customer CMK.

KMS integration: require CMEK/CSEK support. They want BYOK flow: import key or use CloudHSM-backed CMK; Redwood must provide key-wrapping workflow and documented key-rotation steps. Need proof for HSM attestation.

Key rotation policy: min 90-day rotation for data-encryption keys; monthly rotation for short-lived signing keys if used. Rotation must not break cached KV tokens; require key aliasing and key versioning support.

Secrets management: recommend HashiCorp Vault integration or Redwood-managed secrets stored in customer VPC-only secrets store. Auto-rotate connector credentials; ephemeral credentials preferred for storage/S3 access.

Audit logging / telemetry: all KMS calls (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/Rotate) must be logged and forwarded to customer SIEM (Splunk) + retained for 12 months initially. Access to audit logs via secure log collector endpoint or S3 with MFA delete option.
Compliance ask: must surface cryptographic module FIPS 140-2/3 validated libs for any HSM-backed ops; SOC2 readiness materials requested (we provided SOC2 Type II summary doc in drive link).

Operational considerations: need runbook for key compromise (procedure to re-encrypt caches, revoke grants, rotate aliases) and test harness for failover when KMS unavailable (offline fallback policy).

Performance/latency concerns: they worry KMS round-trip for every token decrypt will add tail latency. Discussed envelope encryption + local data-key cache with strict TTL (30s-5m) and cache invalidation on rotation.

Canary/fallback policy: they want partial fallback to a lower-capacity hosted model only if private capacity exhausted, but legal prefers that fallback still honor data residency and not send PHI to hosted environments — currently blocker.
Quote from Head of Security: "We can't hand over key material; HSM-backed BYOK or customer-managed KMS is non-negotiable. Also need proof that audit logs can't be tampered with."

Action items recorded: (1) Provide KMS integration spec + sample IAM policies; (2) Provide runbook for rotation and compromise; (3) Share network diagram showing no plaintext egress; (4) Demo Vault connector with token rotation.
